name: GSAP Radial Stagger
description: Wavefront grid expansion driven by gsap.utils.distribute({ from: 'center' }). Each cell receives a per-position delay proportional to its distance from the grid origin, producing a radial reveal CSS keyframes cannot express because animation-delay is a static per-element value, not derivable from 2D position. No GSAP plugins required — uses core distribute() with the grid + from + amount + ease arguments.

rows.description: Grid rows. The total cell count is rows × cols; keep under ~50 cells to avoid DOM perf hits during capture.

amount.description: Total stagger time (seconds). Distribute() spreads this across all cells from origin to edges.

from.description: Origin keyword: 'center', 'edges', 'start', 'end', 'random', or a [row, col] tuple. See gsap.utils.distribute docs.

distribute_ease.description: Ease applied to the distance-to-delay mapping itself — controls whether the wavefront accelerates or decelerates as it propagates.

when_to_use: Grid reveals where the wavefront direction carries meaning (e.g. content radiating from a focal point)
Hero entrances that should feel kinetic and physics-driven without being literally physical
Montage scenes where coordinated multi-element entry establishes scale or volume
when_to_avoid: Sequential reveals where reading order matters — readers track left-to-right, not center-out
Editorial scenes — the radial pattern reads too kinetic for content-forward registers
Tutorials — distracts from the focused-attention model neutral-light demands
ai_guidance: Distinctive GSAP-only choreography. The hook is gsap.utils.distribute with grid + from arguments — drives per-element delays from 2D position. Uses core GSAP, no plugins required. The capture pipeline auto-attaches the GSAP adapter when window.gsap is present. For React/ESM prototypes, call window.__animaticSyncGsap?.(gsap) once after import. See prototype_template for the complete pattern.
